'''Hao Helen Zhang''' is a Chinese statistician. She is a professor at the [[University of Arizona]], in the Department of Mathematics, Statistics Interdisciplinary Program, and Applied Mathematics Interdisciplinary Program there.{{r|cv}} With Bertrand Clarke and Ernest Fokoué, she is the author of the book ''Principles and Theory for Data Mining and Machine Learning''.{{r|ptdmml}}

Zhang earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics in 1996 from [[Peking University]]. She completed her Ph.D. in statistics in 2002 from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[Grace Wahba]], was ''Nonparametric Variable Selection and Model Building Via Likelihood Basis Pursuit''.{{r|mgp}} She joined the Department of Statistics at [[North Carolina State University]] in 2002, and moved to Arizona in 2011.{{r|cv}}

Zhang was elected to the [[International Statistical Institute]] and as a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] in 2015. She became a fellow in the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2016, and has been selected as the 2019 Medallion Lecturer of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.{{r|cv}}
